A US federal appeals court has rejected the Trump administration’s policy of rapidly deporting migrants to countries other than their own – a ruling that could next go before the Supreme Court.
On Friday, a three-judge panel of the 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals in Boston largely upheld a February decision that found the Department of Homeland Security’s so-called third-country removal policy unlawful.

The case stems from a class-action lawsuit testing what due process migrants are owed before being sent to nations with which they have no ties.
Writing for the panel, US Circuit Judge Seth Aframe said migrants must be given a “meaningful” chance to raise safety concerns before removal, rejecting the Trump administration’s narrower reading of the law.
The court did overturn part of the ruling on procedural grounds, concerning whether officials must first try deporting migrants to countries they have ties to.
Trina Realmuto, a lawyer for the plaintiffs at the National Immigration Litigation Alliance, said the decision confirmed that “due process and the protections Congress enacted against persecution and torture cannot be circumvented by putting someone on a plane to a country that was never part of their removal proceedings”.
The DHS did not immediately comment. The Trump administration is expected to appeal the ruling.
Under Trump, the US has struck agreements allowing it to send more than 25,000 migrants to at least 29 third countries, most often Mexico, according to Third Country Deportation Watch, a tracker run by the rights groups Refugees International and Human Rights First.
The policy, adopted in March 2025, allowed removals with only minimal notice if officials had diplomatic assurances against persecution.
The controversial programme has reached the Supreme Court twice.
In 2025, the justices cleared the way for eight men, including nationals of Cuba, Myanmar and Vietnam, to be deported to South Sudan, a country the US State Department advises against visiting because of “crime, kidnapping, and armed conflict”.
The DHS called the removals “a win”, while rights groups said they flouted basic protections.
The Trump administration’s immigration agenda has faced a string of setbacks this month.
A federal judge blocked planned caps on student and journalist visas, calling the government’s justification “exceptionally weak”, while a coalition of 22 states and Washington, DC, sued to stop a separate rule that would let officials deny green cards to immigrants who lawfully use public benefits.

local stone, brick and terracotta screens layer across three-story gathering space in indonesia
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
02:10:53 UTC
11:10:53 KST

Local stone and perforated brick shape Common Days in Maros
Located in Maros, a small town on the outskirts of Makassar, Indonesia, Common Days by INS Studio occupies a newly developed commercial district where the urban fabric remains relatively sparse, allowing the surrounding natural landscape to remain a defining presence. Conceived as a gathering space, the building is organized across three levels, each accommodating a distinct program while collectively encouraging social interaction, work, and community activities.
From the earliest stages of the design process, the architects envisioned a three-story building crowned by an open-air rooftop garden. This decision was driven by the site’s orientation toward Bukit Cenrana, a hill that has long served as one of Maros’ most recognizable natural landmarks. Elevating the building above its surroundings allows visitors to enjoy uninterrupted views of the landscape, transforming the scenery into an integral part of the architectural experience rather than merely a backdrop. The project also embraces a strong sense of locality through its careful selection of materials and craftsmanship. Locally sourced andesite stone, harvested from nearby mountains, becomes the dominant interior material, appearing across walls, flooring, and the coffee bar in a distinctive square pattern. Terracottabrick perforated screens shape a tactile, climate-responsive exterior skin. These natural textures establish a tactile connection between the architecture and its surrounding landscape while reinforcing the building’s regional identity.
climate-responsive facade connects Common Days to Maros’ hills
The ground floor functions as a coffee shop, designed as the social heart of the building. Its open spatial arrangement encourages visitors to gather, while maintaining a seamless visual and physical connection to the second floor, where the atmosphere shifts toward a quieter working environment. Dedicated to productivity and collaboration, the second floor accommodates a working space alongside private meeting rooms for indoor activities. Extending from the interior is an outdoor terrace finished predominantly with locally produced terracotta bricks, creating a warm and familiar architectural expression. A striking moss wall introduces greenery into the workspace, providing a calming visual element that enhances comfort and well-being for visitors throughout the day. The moss itself was cultivated and installed by local gardeners, further emphasizing the project’s commitment to supporting local craftsmanship and resources. The terrace also highlights the use of locally manufactured brick, reinforcing the architectural narrative of place.
One of the building’s defining facade elements is a perforated breeze block wall that serves both environmental and aesthetic purposes. Beyond establishing a strong visual identity, the screen filters the intense morning sunlight that reaches the front elevation while allowing natural ventilation to flow freely from the surrounding hills into the second-floor terrace and beyond. This passive environmental strategy continues to the rooftop garden, an open space designed not only for relaxation but also as a flexible venue for small exhibitions, community gatherings, and outdoor events. Together with the panoramic views of Bukit Cenrana, the rooftop becomes the culmination of the spatial journey through the building, where architecture and landscape converge. Rather than imposing an unfamiliar architectural language, Common Days project by INS Studio responds to the character of Maros through a contemporary interpretation of local materials, climate-responsive design, and meaningful engagement with the surrounding landscape. As the town continues to grow, the building demonstrates how architecture can accommodate new ways of gathering and working while remaining deeply rooted in the identity and cultural context of its place.

Chinese scientists find first evidence of ancient nose-chopping punishment for cattle thieves
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
02:00:10 UTC
11:00:10 KST

Chinese scientists find first evidence of ancient nose-chopping punishment for cattle thieves
Under the rule of the King of Qin (247 BC–221 BC), severed noses accumulated like mountain peaks, and carts overflowed with amputated feet
Stealing someone’s cattle is a serious crime, and in many places, the thief would end up in jail. However, ancient Chinese justice could result in a truly horrific form of mutilation: the amputation of the nose.
This harsh consequence has been well-documented by historians as one of the infamous “five punishments” from the penal system of the Xia dynasty (2070 BC–1600 BC). Until now, no physical evidence of this punishment had been discovered.
A team of researchers from China and the US recently announced the finding of a female skeleton dated between 1298 and 1404 (from either the Yuan or Ming dynasties) that showed clear evidence of nose removal as part of a criminal sentence.

Harry Kane (front) of Bayern Munich takes a penalty to score during the German first division Bundesliga football match between FC Bayern Munich and 1. FC Union Berlin in Munich, Germany, Sept. 18, 2026. (Photo by Philippe Ruiz/Xinhua)
BERLIN, Sept. 18 (Xinhua) -- Harry Kane became the fastest player to score 100 Bundesliga goals, while Michael Olise hit a hat-trick as Bayern Munich thrashed Union Berlin 7-0 on Friday.
Union, with captain Christopher Trimmel replacing the ill Josip Juranovic, defended deep under coach Mauro Lustrinelli and kept Bayern at bay during the opening 15 minutes.
Jamal Musiala broke the deadlock in the 18th minute, drilling a low shot into the right corner for his first Bundesliga goal since Bayern's 4-3 win over Mainz on April 25.
Union goalkeeper Frederik Ronnow produced a sharp save to deny Jonathan Tah before Olise won a penalty after being fouled by Tom Rothe inside the area in the 38th minute. Kane converted from the spot a minute later to score his 100th Bundesliga goal in just his 98th appearance, setting a competition record.
Olise made it 3-0 in the 43rd minute, firing into the top corner after receiving a pass from Musiala.
Manuel Neuer was called into action twice shortly after the restart, denying Janik Haberer and Rothe, but Bayern soon resumed its dominance. Olise crossed for Kane to head home his 101st Bundesliga goal in the 54th minute.
Kane was denied a hat-trick by a defensive block, while Rothe cleared substitute Ismael Saibari's effort off the line. Saibari responded moments later, collecting a pass from Alphonso Davies, beating several defenders and firing Bayern's fifth goal into the net in the 70th minute.
Olise then took center stage. Tom Bischof released the Frenchman, who rounded Ronnow to score his second goal three minutes later. The same pair combined again in the 76th minute, with Olise curling the ball home to complete his hat-trick and seal the 7-0 rout.
Serge Gnabry came off the bench in the 77th minute as Bayern comfortably saw out the closing stages.
"Top performance on the highest level from start to finish. To reach 101 Bundesliga goals makes me proud," Kane said.
Union remains without a victory after four rounds, while Bayern will travel to Augsburg after the international break. Union will host newly promoted Elversberg on October 10. ■

====================================================================================================

Google's Gemini becomes latest AI model to break out and hack computer systems
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
01:41:49 UTC
10:41:49 KST

Google said on Friday that its Gemini model had hacked three other companies, the first time the search giant has disclosed that one of its models autonomously gained access to third-party computer systems without permission.
In May, the Gemini model accessed three separate private computer systems by guessing passwords and by twice using a repository of publicly listed passwords, Google said.
The incident happened as part of a "capture-the-flag" security test run by Israeli startup Irregular, and Google's agents were never supposed to access the broader internet, but a bug in the testing environment made internet access available.
The agents stopped their intrusion when they determined they had accessed real company systems, not just part of the testing environment, Google said.
"In a standard evaluation, the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test," Heather Adkins, vice president of security engineering at Google, said in a statement. "In all three of these instances, the model stopped."
The disclosure comes as scrutiny over misbehaving artificial intelligence intensifies in Washington and Silicon Valley.
OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta have in recent weeks reported incidents where their AI models had broken out of their testing environments and attempted to hack other companies to gain unauthorized access to computer systems.
The disclosures of so-called "misaligned" AI models prompted Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to call for the industry to collectively slow down the development of the most advanced AI models until companies can ensure they are safe.
All of the above incidents involved Israeli startup Irregular. The company, which is backed by Sequoia and Redpoint Ventures, was valued last year at $450 million. Its tools help foundation model developers perform cybersecurity tests on their cutting-edge technologies.
An Irregular spokesperson told CNBC that the Google incident was related to the same issue that allowed the other models to access the internet.
"This is the same issue that was already reported and does not represent a materially separate incident," an Irregular spokesperson said in a statement. "All relevant labs were notified in late July, and affected entities were contacted as part of the investigation."
Google said the incident happened in May and it was notified by Irregular in late July. Google has worked with Irregular to change its testing process.
A Google spokesperson declined to identify the exact Gemini model involved.
"These events highlight the importance of training powerful AI models to act responsibly," Google's Adkins said in a statement.
The Wall Street Journal first reported the security incident.
CNBC's Jonathan Vanian contributed reporting.

Anthropic picks Accenture for in-house AI safety evaluation
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
01:40:00 UTC
10:40:00 KST

Anthropic picks Accenture for in-house AI safety evaluation
NEW YORK – Anthropic said it is partnering with consulting giant Accenture to have outside evaluators work inside the artificial intelligence company, a step towards fulfilling a pledge by chief executive Dario Amodei to have independent observers evaluate its most powerful models.
The partnership will be led by Faculty, Accenture’s specialist AI business. Its work will include evaluating and “red-teaming” Anthropic’s models, the company said on Sept 18.
Red-teaming is the practice of deliberately trying to make AI systems misbehave to expose flaws.
Anthropic and Accenture each expect to invest at least US$1 billion (S$1.28 billion) over the next five years for the effort.
The pledge was made in a Sept 12 essay in which Amodei argued that AI companies must slow the pace at which they improve their models’ capabilities.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has said his company would give outside evaluators similar access, while Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella welcomed embedded evaluators but cautioned that a handful of entities should not control oversight.
Given the “importance and urgency of this work”, Anthropic said it will fund Accenture’s work directly, but that in the long term, “funding should come from pooled or government sources”.
Anthropic said it is in talks with Model Evaluation and Threat Research (METR), a California-based non-profit organisation, to participate in elements of embedded evaluation using METR’s own funding.
Critics, including David Sacks, a former White House AI adviser, have questioned METR’s independence because of its ties to Anthropic’s investors and staff.
METR says it takes no funding from AI companies or their executives.
On Sept 18, more than 100 AI researchers, including Geoffrey Hinton, who is considered an AI “godfather”, signed a public letter calling for evaluators embedded in AI companies to be “meaningfully independent”.
That includes, at a minimum, that such organisations “should not be owned or governed by frontier AI companies, should not have other significant commercial business with them, and should not accept any form of payment or other reward contingent on the evaluator’s findings”, the letter said. AFP

UN documents more than 1,000 cases of sexual violence since start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
01:36:00 UTC
10:36:00 KST

UN documents more than 1,000 cases of sexual violence since start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine
This is stated in a report by the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights released on Friday, according to Ukrinform.
“Some 1,004 cases of sexual violence were documented from 24 February 2022, when Russia’s attack on Ukraine began, through to the end of July this year. Of these cases, 89 percent were attributed to Russian authorities - including members of the armed forces, the prison service and the national security service. The remaining 11 percent were attributed to Ukrainian authorities,” the report states.
The report, “Sexual Violence in the Context of the Russian Federation’s Full-Scale Armed Attack on Ukraine,” is based on confidential interviews with hundreds of victims and survivors of sexual violence, as well as other relevant materials, including court documents and official records.
It notes that the majority of victims of sexual violence were men, especially in places of detention; however, women and children were also affected, primarily in the occupied territory of Ukraine. Documented violations include gang rape, rape, genital mutilation, electric shock to the genitals, and beatings of the genitals, as well as other degrading acts of a sexual nature. The youngest documented survivor of rape was a four-year-old girl, and the oldest was an 82-year-old woman. In both cases, the sexual violence was committed by representatives of Russian authorities, according to the report.
Many men who survived sexual violence reported that they were electrocuted in the genital area using a Soviet military field telephone known as a “tapik.”
“The application of electric shocks to genitals with a “tapik” or taser was a common form of sexual violence used against Ukrainian POWs and retained medical personnel, with 155 (27 per cent) having endured this form at least once,” the report states.
According to the report, nearly half of the violations attributed to Ukrainian authorities regarding Russian prisoners of war and prisoners of war who are citizens of third countries consisted of threats of sexual violence.
“Sexual violence is a grave feature of the full-scale armed attack against Ukraine. It must stop immediately, irrespective of the perpetrators. Given the high prevalence of cases attributed to its forces, however, the Russian Federation in particular must take concrete and discernible steps to protect civilians and prisoners of war from all forms of torture, including sexual violence,” stated UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk.
He called on Russia to immediately, completely, and unconditionally cease the use of force against Ukraine and withdraw all its armed forces from Ukrainian territory in accordance with the UN Charter and binding norms of international law.
As reported by Ukrinform, Germany condemned Russia’s systematic human rights violations in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine and called for an immediate end to the torture of prisoners and the return of abducted Ukrainian children.

Japan’s wartime kamikaze pilots remain among the most recognisable symbols of the Pacific war: young men flying aircraft into Allied ships on missions from which they were not expected to return.
Far less well-remembered are the fukuryu – suicide frogmen trained in the closing months of World War II to walk into the sea with mines on bamboo poles, then wait beneath the waves for an Allied invasion fleet.
Kanade Hamamoto was one of many Japanese people who had never heard of them, despite spending years on the same stretch of coast where they once trained.
The 25-year-old photographer knew Inamuragasaki, on the Shonan coast south of Tokyo, only as a scenic seaside spot until a friend mentioned that the remains of a military base could still be seen near the cape, in tunnels cut into the cliff face.

Hong Kong’s first five-year plan marks a new chapter for the city and will prompt discussion about individual priorities and initiatives. But there is another question worth asking: what can Hong Kong bring to the national journey over the next five years?

Trump signs broad Russia sanctions bill
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
01:27:00 UTC
10:27:00 KST

Trump signs broad Russia sanctions bill
September 19, 2026
US President Donald Trump signed into law a package of new sanctions against Russia named after the late Senator Lindsey Graham, the White House said on Friday.
Earlier, the bill passed Congress with large bipartisan majorities: 86-11 in the Senate and 262-159 in the House.
The comprehensive sanctions package is intended to punish and pressure Moscow for its ongoing war against Ukraine.
In addition to the sanctions on Russia, the law establishes a framework to maintain sanctions on Iran until 2031.
What sanctions does the bill include?
The bill targets Russian officials and key sectors of the Russian economy, including banks, and a fleet of shadow tankers that transport Russian energy.
It also instructs Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five importers of Russian oil or natural gas. However, some countries are exempt.
The US president can also impose sanctions on the five countries that do the most to help Russia circumvent energy sanctions.
These measures could further strain US trade relations with China and India, both of which buy significant amounts of Russian oil.
What are the reactions?
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy thanked Trump for signing the bill, as well as all the senators and members of the House of Representatives who supported it.
"When Lindsey Graham was here in Ukraine, he would always talk about how important it was not to ease pressure on Russia, to strengthen sanctions and seek a path to peace," he wrote on X.
Graham, who played a leading role in advancing the bill, was a staunch supporter of Ukraine. The senator had just returned from Ukraine when he unexpectedly passed away in July.
"The best way to honor Lindsey's memory will be to implement the provisions of this law fully and swiftly. And the best reward for everyone helping us put pressure on Russia to end its war will be peace," Zelenskyy added.
Before Trump signed the bill, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov warned that additional US sanctions would hinder efforts to achieve a peaceful resolution in Ukraine.

6
 Listen
The Iran war has cost US$43.6 billion as of this month, the highest official estimate to date, the Pentagon told Congress’ defence oversight panels this week.
The cost estimate comes as polls show Americans increasingly oppose the war, partly over its impact on the economy, and the issue is looming large as the November midterm elections approach.
The Pentagon’s latest figure comprises US$11.2 billion already obliged for operating expenses – for fuel, combat pay, aircraft, medical care, parts and the like – plus US$32.4 billion in unfunded replacement costs for munitions, damaged aircraft and other assets, according to a Pentagon document submitted to Congress.
The estimate does not include the cost of addressing potentially billions of dollars in damages to US military facilities in eight Middle East countries.

====================================================================================================

The world is arguing about migration. Here's where Australia fits
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
00:56:31 UTC
09:56:31 KST

IN BRIEF
- Australia is targeting students, backpackers and overstayers as it seeks to bring net overseas migration down.
- Canada, the US, UK and countries across Europe are also tightening parts of their immigration systems.
Australia has unveiled a major shake-up of its migration system, targeting visa-hoppers, overstayers, international students and backpackers as the federal government seeks to bring migration down further.
The changes come as governments in several other major migrant destinations — including Canada, the United Kingdom, the United States and Europe — also tighten parts of their immigration systems.
Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke announced the reforms on Thursday, which include restrictions on international students bringing family members, new rules aimed at preventing "visa hopping", and caps on working holidaymakers seeking to extend their stays.
The government is also strengthening enforcement against visa overstayers and migration agents who lodge applications without merit, while changing the skilled migration system to prioritise workers in areas including healthcare, construction and education.
The government wants to bring net overseas migration down from 292,100 to 245,000 in the year to July 2027, and to 225,000 each year thereafter.
News that makes sense
Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.
The changes include caps on working holidaymakers extending their stays, with 45,000 second-year places and just 5,000 third-year places — down from 57,000 and 31,000 respectively.
There will also be a crackdown on the 77,000 people who are believed to be overstaying their visas: they will face tougher enforcement, including detention.
So, how does Australia's approach compare with migration changes elsewhere in the world?
The United States
The United States has pursued what US President Donald Trump has promised to be the "largest domestic deportation" operation in US history, built on aggressive enforcement.
Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has been tasked with that crackdown after its annual budget more than tripled, with heavily armed agents facing worldwide backlash for aggressive tactics, including the fatal shootings of two US citizens this year in Minneapolis.
The Department of Homeland Security says the Trump administration has deported more than 605,000 "illegal aliens", with a further 1.9 million "self-deporting".
Trump has also focused on border security, particularly in the south, primarily targeting Mexican migrants and those crossing the border illegally — as well as the construction of the continued and expanded construction of the Mexico-United States border wall.
He has also worked to restrict the entry of foreigners who do follow the rules and has gone after those who overstay their visas after they expire.
The US government plans to revoke the visas of foreigners who came to the country for tourism or business but sought to stay longer by applying for asylum.
The administration also paused visa approvals for people from 75 "high-risk" countries — Afghanistan, Brazil, Egypt, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Somalia, Thailand and Yemen — a move a federal judge struck down last month.
He also saw another legal setback this week after a federal judge blocked his attempt to impose stricter limits on how long foreign students and journalists can study or work in the US.
The Trump administration has also expanded vetting of visa applicants' social media accounts, with a State Department spokesperson saying: "A visa is a privilege — not a right."
In August, the department said that since President Donald Trump returned to power in January 2025, some 175,000 foreigners had seen their US visas revoked on grounds ranging from criminal offences, including driving under the influence, to praising the killing of the right-wing activist Charlie Kirk.
Canada
Canada has long held a reputation for welcoming immigrants, with foreign-born people making up almost a quarter of its population.
But that reputation, and its appeal relative to the US' immigration crackdown under Trump, hasn't stopped Canada from hardening its own approach.
Under Prime Minister Mark Carney, Canada has cut its temporary resident target to 385,000 this year, down 25 per cent from the 516,600 previously planned for 2026.
Canada aims to reduce its temporary resident population to less than 5 per cent of the total population by the end of 2027.
Of the 385,000 temporary resident arrivals targeted this year, 230,000 are workers and 155,000 are international students.
International students have been particularly affected by Canada's migration tightening. The government expects to issue up to 408,000 study permits in 2026 — including extensions for existing students — down 7 per cent from its 2025 target and 16 per cent from its 2024 target.
Canada's temporary population has already begun to fall, declining from a peak of 7.6 per cent of the country's population to 6.5 per cent.
Immigration plans for 2026-28 focus on a "return to sustainable immigration levels", with a focus on decreasing temporary resident arrivals and stabilising permanent resident admissions.
While reducing temporary migration, Canada plans to stabilise permanent migration at 380,000 admissions a year between 2026 and 2028.
Its plan places greater emphasis on economic migration and workers in high-demand occupations, while continuing to prioritise family reunification and refugee resettlement.
Canada is also increasing its target for French-speaking permanent residents settling outside Quebec, from 9 per cent of admissions in 2026 to 9.5 per cent in 2027 and 10.5 per cent in 2028.
It will also focus on attracting workers in high-demand occupations and increase the target for Francophone admissions, while aiming to continue to be a "global leader in refugees" and prioritise family reunification.
Former prime minister Justin Trudeau sought to attract more immigrants to the country, but the increase in migration was blamed for housing pressure and unemployment rates, resulting in a sharp cut in the number of immigrants allowed into the country.
The United Kingdom
The United Kingdom is also moving to tighten its migration system, with the government proposing to double the standard qualifying period for permanent settlement from five to 10 years.
Under an "earned settlement" model, some legal migrants could face waits of up to 20 years, depending on factors including their reliance on benefits, while high earners and other applicants deemed to have made significant contributions could qualify sooner.
The proposals could affect an estimated 2.6 million people who arrived in the UK since 2021, while separate reforms to the asylum system would replace permanent refugee status with temporary status subject to review every 30 months.
Europe
Europe is cracking down harder on migration amid rising anti-immigration rhetoric in recent years, the surging popularity of far-right parties, and unfolding humanitarian crises.
In June, the European Parliament approved a new migration plan that would allow the return of illegally staying third-country nationals, with the possibility of detention if they don't comply.
The same law doubles detention times for irregular migrants, speeds up deportations, toughens entry bans, and gives authorities the power to search migrants' homes.
One of the changes includes the creation of so-called "return hubs", which would see migrants without legal residency, including rejected asylum seeker claims, hosted in centres in non-EU nations — a model the Lowy Institute says borrows from Australia's own offshore detention approach.
Five countries — Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands — are working on the "return hub" plan, with Denmark's immigration minister saying he expects to send the first people to a partner country by the end of 2027.
But not every EU member is on board, with French President Emmanuel Macron dismissing the approach as ineffective and out of step with European values.
The push lands amid a broader rightward shift on migration across Europe.
In Germany, far-right political party Alternative for Germany (AfD) — who vow to heavily restrict immigration — topped state elections, putting a far-right party within reach of power at the state level for the first time since World War II.
Swedish elections on Thursday saw the centre-left Social Democrats win a slim majority — but they have still vowed to maintain a hardline immigration policy, inspired by their Danish counterparts who have one of Europe's toughest and most restrictive immigration policies.
Spain, meanwhile, is dealing with its own migrant humanitarian crisis after at least 72,000 people crossed into the North African enclave of Ceuta from Morocco in July. More than 10,000 migrants remain stranded.
Just this week, the European Commission pitched a new emergency response framework following the Ceuta crisis, which could translate into a temporary suspension of the right to asylum in the event of "mass movements" which are "engineered and weaponised".

CBI immediately lodged an FIR and laid a trap just hours later, catching the intermediary.The intermediary, who alleged that he accepted the bribe on behalf of the official, was given a pardon.SC said since the FIR was lodged on Aug 4, 2005, at 2pm and CBI decided to lay the trap on the same day, the agency must have verified the authenticity of the complaint before the trap was planned. "It is surprising that CBI started the investigation of a cognisable offence by way of verifying the complaint of bribery even before the formal FIR was lodged...
The entire trap was arranged between 2 pm to 4.30pm. While the investigating agency cannot be faulted for organising the trap in such an extraordinarily speedy manner, it can raise certain doubts. The trial court, however, brushed aside the doubts raised by the appellant," the bench said.
The court said criminality under Prevention of Corruption Act did not arise merely because money changed hands. "Before criminal liability can be fastened upon the public servant, the prosecution must establish by reliable evidence that the intermediary was acting under the authority, direction or for the benefit of the accused and that the demand itself was attributable to the accused. Mere receipt of money by a third person cannot automatically result in criminal liability being imputed to a public servant," it said.

The court said recent hooch tragedies in Bhavnagar (Gujarat) and Sagar (MP), which claimed 13 and 15 lives respectively, were a reminder for the authorities to wake up and act."History bears eloquent testimony to the fact that complete alcohol ban often drives the liquor trade underground, increasing the prevalence of unregulated, lethal brews. The state of Gujarat has a strict prohibition policy... It has witnessed at least 10 major mass hooch tragedies since the state's formation and independence, claiming the lives of over 600 people," the bench said.
SC rejected Maharashtra govt's plea and said the rules had no rational nexus with the objective sought to be achieved to prevent hooch tragedies. The court said it was not doubting the intention of the state but intention solely would not pass the test of manifest arbitrariness."The state failed to indicate that this practice of putting such additives would discourage or rather dissuade continuous usage of methanol or affect its chemical composition so it cannot be used in making spurious liquor. Further, the state has also failed to indicate how mixing of the additives would definitively prevent deaths. Another question that is left unanswered is how the respondent plans to prevent manufacturing of spurious liquor by the use of other adulterants," the bench said.

Trump signs sweeping Russia sanctions over Ukraine war
New law allows tariffs of up to 100 percent on major buyers of Russian oil, including China and India.
US President Donald Trump has signed into law a sweeping sanctions package targeting Russia over its war in Ukraine, days after Congress sent the bill to the White House with rare bipartisan support.
Signed on Friday, the legislation, known as the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, honours the late Republican senator who spent more than a year negotiating it before his sudden death in July. It was co-written with Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal.
Recommended Stories

The bill sanctions Russian President Vladimir Putin, senior officials and oligarchs, along with Russian banks and financial institutions. It also targets Moscow’s energy and defence sectors and the so-called shadow fleet of tankers used to move Russian oil around Western sanctions.
A key provision gives Trump authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 percent on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas, a measure expected to fall hardest on China and India, the top two importers of Russian crude. The bill separately extends sanctions on Iran’s energy and weapons sectors.
The bill passed the Senate last month and the House on Wednesday, with 58 Democrats crossing party lines to back it.
It marks the first major Ukraine-related bill to clear Congress in more than two years.
Supporters say the aim is to starve the Kremlin of the funds sustaining its war effort and push Putin towards negotiations. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who had lobbied lawmakers ahead of the vote, called the legislation “an extremely powerful tool”.
House Speaker Mike Johnson said the bill placed “maximum pressure” on what he called “the Russian war machine”, while Blumenthal said he hoped it would help bring Moscow to the table, telling Putin: “We have your number.”
Not all Democrats were on board. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries opposed the bill, warning that its tariff powers would raise costs for American families and calling its sanctions provisions full of “loopholes”.
India, one of the countries most exposed to the new tariff threat, said this week that it “remains firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people”.
Trump’s decision comes about a week before he is due to host Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House.

Anthropic considers releasing new AI model ahead of IPO, sources say
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
00:40:00 UTC
09:40:00 KST

Anthropic considers releasing new AI model ahead of IPO, sources say
Anthropic is considering rolling out a new AI model to counter OpenAI’s momentum since its competitor’s launch of GPT-6 Astra, according to three sources, ahead of an expected initial public offering (IPO) and after its CEO called for an industrywide slowdown.
The timing of a potential launch aimed at addressing competitive pressure from a direct rival follows Anthropic chief executive officer Dario Amodei’s call on the global AI community to slow down the pace of releasing new capabilities to address safety concerns, the sources said.
“We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models,” he wrote in a 3,800-word essay on Sept 12.
The essay, which painted a bleak picture of swarms of AI agents taking over the internet and outpacing human control, drew support from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.
OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, released this month, has gained traction among businesses, prompting concerns among some investors who told Reuters they are re-evaluating Anthropic’s position as the leading provider of enterprise AI tools.
Anthropic is evaluating the safety of its next model as part of its deliberations over a release, one of the people familiar with the matter said.
Some of the discussions involve how to balance investment in releasing new models with efforts to strengthen the company’s profitability as rising interest rates make investors more focused on the timing of expected profits, said people familiar with the company’s thinking.
The debate over spending highlights the increasing pressure on the firms at the centre of the AI boom to produce sustainable cash flows sooner, thanks both to rising rates and tough competition from open-source AI providers, especially in China.
Anthropic declined to comment for this story.
The potential launch would test how Anthropic can defend its enterprise market position against OpenAI while maintaining the safety-first identity that has distinguished it from competitors.
OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra gains enterprise traction
OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra on Sept 3, touting gains in computer use, software engineering, cybersecurity and professional work.
The model has received a strong response from enterprise users and developers, prompting potential Anthropic IPO investors to scrutinise whether OpenAI could begin taking market share from Anthropic, which has been viewed for months as the leader in enterprise AI.
Astra accounted for about 13 per cent of enterprise AI spending tracked by corporate expense platform Ramp, compared with about 8 per cent for Anthropic’s Claude Fable, according to the latest data.
Astra has also pulled ahead on OpenRouter, a widely used platform that routes developer traffic across AI models. 
OpenRouter said its users spent more on OpenAI models than on Anthropic models last week, the first time OpenAI has led on that measure in more than 2½ years.
Anthropic maintains revenue advantage
Some existing investors and those who expect to invest in both Anthropic’s and OpenAI’s IPOs said they do not believe Astra poses a significant threat to Anthropic, given the size of its lead in the market for enterprise AI tools and the amount of time it takes to unseat incumbent vendors to large companies.
Anthropic’s annualised revenue run rate topped US$65 billion by the end of July, up from about US$9 billion at the end of 2025. 
It is also projecting a 2028 revenue of roughly US$190 billion to US$200 billion, Reuters previously reported. 
OpenAI’s annualised revenue run rate passed US$40 billion in July.
Investors also expect leadership among Anthropic, OpenAI, Alphabet’s Google and other major AI developers to shift repeatedly as companies release new generations of models, making any advantage potentially short-lived.
Bigger challenges ahead
A potentially bigger challenge for Anthropic and other leading AI providers is the rise of open-source and open-weight models, which can lower token costs and allow companies to build more of their own AI infrastructure rather than rely on providers such as Anthropic and OpenAI, investors said.
The shift could put pressure on the economics of the AI industry as companies have more options to develop and run models outside the leading commercial providers, broadening the competitive threat beyond the race between Anthropic and OpenAI.
Meta Platforms has been among Anthropic’s largest customers, but is looking to reduce its use of Anthropic’s models as it develops more AI capabilities internally, people familiar with the matter said. 
Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
OpenAI, meanwhile, has taken some pressure off the race to public markets. 
Its CEO, Altman, confirmed on Sept 12 that the company would not go public in 2026, saying concerns around AI safety made this an ill-advised time for a listing.
Anthropic could push its IPO to after the November US midterm elections, with the elections not expected to have a major impact on the offering, according to two people familiar with the matter. 
The IPO has already been pushed back from earlier plans, with Reuters previously reporting that marketing was expected to begin in mid-October at the earliest. REUTERS

South Korea, US discuss Seoul’s role in Middle East and investment pact
WASHINGTON – South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun met US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Sept 18 as the long-time allies grappled with delayed South Korean investments in the US and Seoul’s role in Middle East security.
US President Donald Trump has criticised Seoul in recent weeks over what he described as a lack of South Korean support for US efforts to pressure Iran.
The two countries have also yet to finalise agreements governing US$350 billion (S$446.4 billion) in South Korean investments pledged under a trade deal reached in 2025.
Cho explained to Rubio Seoul’s willingness to make a substantive contribution to restoring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, the ministry said in a statement without elaborating.
On Seoul’s investment commitments, Rubio stressed their swift execution, the US State Department said, while South Korea’s Foreign Ministry said Rubio and Cho agreed to keep communicating to ensure ongoing consultation plans “bear good fruit”.
Rubio and Cho also pledged ongoing collaboration across key strategic sectors, including semiconductors, the State Department said, while Rubio underscored the need for a fair and transparent business environment for US companies in South Korea.
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, who is due in the US next week for the UN General Assembly, said on Sept 18 that he would not deploy military assets to the Middle East in a way that could draw the country into a conflict.
But he said Seoul was reviewing whether to play a greater role in safeguarding navigation in the region.
Cho said before leaving Seoul on Sept 17 that investment plans under the trade deal had been delayed while procedural issues were clarified, without elaborating.
Lee told a news conference on Sept 18 that concerns over the commercial viability of the package had become a sticking point in negotiations, although the two sides were nearing an agreement.
He said some elements of the package were difficult for Seoul to accept, but the government would continue discussions to ensure any deal protected South Korea’s interests while benefiting both countries and the broader US-South Korea relationship.
Seoul committed in 2025 to invest in US manufacturing in return for lowering tariffs on imports from South Korea to 15 per cent.
Lee said Seoul had insisted on including a reference to “commercially reasonable” investments in the text of the agreement.
North Korea also featured in the talks, amid speculation over a possible summit between Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
Rubio and Cho reaffirmed their commitment to the complete denuclearisation of North Korea, the State Department said, while Cho said Seoul would actively support the resumption of talks between Washington and Pyongyang, according to the ministry.
Lee said on Sept 18 that a summit meeting between Kim and Trump could take place in the coming months, but it remained uncertain. REUTERS

Trump extends push for $128,000 H-1B visas by another year
WASHINGTON – President Donald Trump has extended an executive order that would impose a fee of US$100,000 (S$128,000) for H-1B non-immigrant visas by another year, the White House said on Sept 18.
US employers seeking to hire skilled foreign workers can use the federal government’s H-1B visa programme for a fee, allowing tech and other professionals from abroad to work in the United States for a few years.
Trump, who has pursued an aggressive immigration crackdown, has criticised the programme and wants to permanently raise the fee from between US$2,000 and US$5,000 to at least US$100,000, though the attempt has faced legal challenges.
A Boston-based appeals court is reviewing a June decision by a federal judge who deemed the higher fee imposed by the Trump administration illegal and blocked the government from collecting it.
Another court is considering whether a judge properly rejected a challenge to the fee by the US Chamber of Commerce, the largest US business lobbying group.
Trump’s initial order for a fee hike, first released in September 2025, was set to expire in September 2026.
It did not apply to visas granted to foreign citizens already in the United States on student visas, who make up a large share of new H-1B recipients, or to renewals of current visas.
Despite criticism that some companies use the visas to hire lower-paid foreign workers instead of Americans, business groups and companies say they help recruit highly skilled professionals and address a lack of qualified US workers in some industries.
The visas, established by Congress in 1990, are especially critical for tech companies seeking to recruit from India and China.
Changes to how potential visa holders are scrutinised and processed have impacted companies’ hiring and expansion plans, with some top H-1B users, such as Google parent company Alphabet, moving to increase operations in India. REUTERS

Why relying on university students skews global psychological research
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
00:00:31 UTC
09:00:31 KST

An analysis of the World Values Survey (2005-2022) data found that individuals with more education tend to be culturally similar to people from the Anglosphere and Western Europe. Interestingly, education level was not associated with cultural similarities to other large and influential countries such as China, Russia, or India. The paper was published in Nature Communications.
Psychological research has traditionally relied heavily on participants from Western, educated, industrialized, rich, and democratic societies. This is so common that the acronym WEIRD has been coined to refer to such groups. However, this has raised concerns about how well findings on such groups generalize to the wider world. Although cross-national research has expanded substantially, many international studies still depend disproportionately on highly educated participants such as university students.
But are university students, even from non-WEIRD countries, really representative of the wider cultures of the countries they belong to? Education itself is an important source of cultural norms. Formal schooling transmits not only knowledge and skills but also particular values, cognitive styles, and patterns of behavior. Studies have found that higher levels of education tend to be associated with traits typically considered characteristic of WEIRD societies, such as individualism, analytic thinking, nonconformity, and generalized trust.
Socioeconomic status may also contribute to the adoption of WEIRD cultural norms through the endorsement of personal freedom, specific styles of thinking, and the availability of resources needed to experience different cultures. However, education may play a particularly important role in determining what kinds of cultural norms a person will actually adopt.
Study authors Cindel J. M. White and Michael Muthukrishna conducted a study in which they explored whether socioeconomic status is associated with a variety of different cultural traits across 95 countries around the world. They note that processes of colonization, globalization, and the adoption of Western-style institutions have led to the diffusion of WEIRD cultural norms around the world. As a result, highly educated individuals could be expected to be more similar to one another across the world, but to also show patterns of attitudes, traits, and behaviors characteristic of cultures of WEIRD countries, including Anglosphere countries like the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Western Europe more generally.
These researchers analyzed data from the World Values Survey (2005-2022), waves 5-7. The World Values Survey is a long-running international research program that measures people’s values, beliefs, attitudes, and social and political views across countries and cultures. These analyses were based on data from 268,992 participants from 95 different countries.
Study authors report that they excluded from analyses any country or group with fewer than 100 respondents. As a result, the number of countries for which data were available differed between analyses and did not always include all 95 countries.
Participants within each country were grouped into high, middle, and low clusters according to three indicators of socioeconomic status: educational attainment, income, and subjective social status. Next, they used a statistic called the cultural fixation index, which quantifies the overall magnitude of cultural differences between groups across a wide range of traits, to measure cultural distance between people with high and low socioeconomic status in 95 countries. Most importantly, they compared all these groups to the U.S., as a prototypical WEIRD country.
Results showed that, across the whole world, highly educated groups and those with only secondary education were more culturally similar to the U.S. than low-education groups. For example, people with high education in Singapore were as similar to the U.S. culturally as highly educated Australians were. However, people with low levels of education from Singapore were culturally quite distant from the U.S. Highly educated Russians were as similar to Americans as highly educated people from New Zealand. However, this was not the case with Russians with low levels of education. This pattern was found in 70 percent of the analyzed countries.
These results seemed to be specific to education. Cultural similarity to the U.S. did not differ between high- and low-income groups, or between groups differing in subjective social status. Additional analyses showed that this observed association between education and cultural similarity becomes even more pronounced when Sweden, the Netherlands, Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, New Zealand, Andorra, Norway, Germany, and Switzerland were used as the reference category. This indicates that the finding might not be about educated people adopting U.S. culture specifically, but about them adopting cultural traits of WEIRD countries in general. Interestingly, education was not associated with cultural similarities to other large, culturally and politically influential countries such as China, Russia, or India.
“Contrary to modernization theories, income and self-reported subjective status did not show the same pattern of WEIRD cultural similarity. Our results suggest that cross-cultural samples of students or university-educated individuals overrepresent cultural values that are typical of WEIRD countries,” the study authors concluded.
The study contributes to the scientific understanding of cultural differences across the world. However, it should be noted that the study was based on data about self-reported beliefs and behaviors, which may not be identical to beliefs and behaviors people practice in everyday life.
The paper, “Higher education predicts global cultural similarity to WEIRD countries,” was authored by Cindel J. M. White and Michael Muthukrishna.

China makes progress in 3-nm chips without advanced lithography tools
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-19
00:00:21 UTC
09:00:21 KST

China makes progress in 3-nm chips without advanced lithography tools
The breakthrough by the Chinese Academy of Sciences is far from mass production but shows China is tracking the road map of global leaders
Chinese researchers have made early strides in pushing semiconductor processing nodes below 3-nm using older lithography technology, as more advanced extreme ultraviolet lithography (EUV) tools from ASML remain blocked under US sanctions.
The breakthrough marks the latest progress in China’s drive to chart an alternative path to advanced chipmaking amid US export restrictions. Under current export control rules, Dutch equipment giant ASML is barred from selling its state-of-the-art EUV machines – essential for producing chips below the 7-nm node – to Chinese clients.
In the latest development, state-backed Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) has established a preliminary gate-all-around (GAA) device development path using the less advanced deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography, Taiwanese media Digitimes reported on Thursday, citing a speech by Ye Tianchun, a veteran from the academy’s Institute of Microelectronics (IMECAS).
Ye said the institute had finished early integration for stacked nanosheet-channel GAA CMOS transistors using DUV tools. He described the result as a “new early-stage MOS transistor process path for China’s sub-3-nm advanced manufacturing”, according to the Digitimes article.

The rival faction led by Arup was allotted the name 'Democratic Trinamool Congress' and 'envelope' poll symbol. The new party names and symbols for Trinamool factions paved the way for their respective candidates to contest the Oct 6 bypoll to Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats in Bengal as well as Nagaon parliamentary seat in Assam. In Nagaon, the Mamata faction fielded Abdul Salam as an AITC candidate. EC Friday said bereft of its intervention, the returning officers would be bound to reject the nomination papers of candidates fielded by both factions, in view of the interim freeze on AITC's reserved symbol. This, they said, would "deprive the electors of a fair electoral competition and prejudice the outcome of elections". "To protect the democratic rights of the electors, preserve the integrity of the electoral process, and ensure that no candidate or faction is unfairly prejudiced pending a final determination of the dispute", EC ruled that the nomination papers filed by candidates of both factions would not be invalidated, subject to fulfilment of statutory requirements.

Zelenskyy: Carpathians can become energy supplier to EU and help ensure independence from Russia
Ukraine

Zelenskyy: Carpathians can become energy supplier to EU and help ensure independence from Russia
At the first Carpathian Economic Forum, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that the countries in the Carpathian region have significant potential for cooperation in the energy sector and that the Carpathians could become a supplier of electricity to the EU, helping ensure energy independence from Russia.
Source: Office of the President of Ukraine
Quote: "Solar and wind energy. Energy storage. And new interconnectors. And our large underground gas storage facilities. And there is also a proposed Carpathian wind cluster with 1.5 gigawatts of capacity. The Carpathians can become an energy contributor to the European Union – and not only a transit region."
Details: Zelenskyy stressed that implementing such projects will help achieve energy independence from Russia.
Overall, the forum brought together around 1,400 participants from 25 countries, with nearly 400 companies from all countries of the Carpathian Eight represented at the event.
According to the Office of the President, the forum's investment portfolio consists of 95 projects worth more than €42.5 billion in energy, industry, innovative technologies, logistics and other sectors. Of these, 55 projects worth €8 billion are in the Ukrainian Carpathians.
Zelenskyy said that around half of the investment portfolio is made up of energy projects, and this sector should become one of the Carpathian region's main contributions to Europe.
He noted that, given Russia's aggressive policy, it was important to attract more investment, create new opportunities across the region and strengthen it:
"More security. Stronger energy links. Better roads and railways and, of course, ports. Security always depends on our ability to work together – when our systems are connected and our countries cooperate, our protection is stronger too," Zelenskyy emphasised.
Background:
- On 18 September, Zelenskyy announced the creation of a new cooperation format, the Carpathian Eight, bringing together Ukraine and seven European countries in the Carpathian region – Romania, Serbia, Poland, Slovakia, Czechia, Austria and Hungary – as well as the EU.
- The forum is taking place in Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast from 18 to 20 September.
- Among other things, Zelenskyy announced that agreements worth €1 billion would be signed during the economic part of the summit.
- Following the first meeting, Ukraine and representatives of the other countries adopted a declaration of intent to ensure cooperation between the countries of the region, the EU and interested partners, including through the organisation of annual summits.
- They also plan to coordinate efforts to strengthen cross-border cooperation, economic ties, security and sustainable development in the Carpathian region, including by increasing the energy resilience of the countries through the development of electricity, heating and gas infrastructure.

Father of murdered Spanish student arrives in Mexico after suspect detained
MEXICO CITY, Sept 18 - The father of a Spanish exchange student killed in Mexico arrived in the Mexican state of Morelos on Friday to identify his daughter's body, a day after authorities detained a suspect in her murder.
Claudia Tacoronte, a 21-year-old student, died from stab wounds on September 12 in the city of Cuautla after someone tried to steal her cellphone, Mexican authorities have said.
On Thursday evening, authorities announced they had arrested a suspect, identified as Francisco Javier "N."
The case has caused widespread anger in both Mexico and Spain, with students demanding stronger protections for women. Mexico has long struggled with high levels of gender-based violence.
Spanish newspaper El Pais, citing sources close to the investigation, reported that the suspect had confessed to the killing.
The killing is being treated as a femicide, or a killing motivated by gender, the state prosecutor in Morelos said.
Morelos recorded 21 femicides between January and July this year, according to official data, while 380 were registered across Mexico over the same period.
The suspect was due to appear before a judge on Friday afternoon. Fernando Blumenkron, Morelos' state prosecutor, said his office would seek the maximum penalty for femicide — 70 years in prison.
Blumenkron told journalists that the suspect attacked Tacoronte outside a cultural building where she had been attending a conference and staying. The prosecutor said the suspect had a police record for burglaries, and had spent time behind bars.
Tacoronte was a student at Spain's University of Granada and had arrived in mid-August on an exchange program at the Autonomous University of the State of Morelos.
At least four female students at the same Mexican university have been killed in Morelos this year, according to student protesters, and Spain's Foreign Ministry has urged citizens to avoid non-essential travel to the state, citing rising drug-related violence and kidnappings.
The University of Granada has also canceled exchange placements for three students who had been due to study in Morelos next semester. REUTERS

wendell castle’s family home returns through furniture and artifacts at friedman benda
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-18
23:55:25 UTC
08:55:25 KST

designboom attended the opening reception for Wendell Castle: Living at Friedman Benda, where the gallery had taken on the density of a lived-in home. A Kermit the Frog toy sits on Environment (1972), Castle’s colossal stacked-walnut bed and work station, and family home videos play on a small television alongside it. Books lie beside furniture and personal objects turn up between works that now belong to the history of American design. The exhibition‘s scale can be monumental, but the rooms feel inhabited.
Curated by Castle’s daughter, Alison Castle, the exhibition begins with a June 1973 House Beautiful feature on the family’s Scottsville, New York, home. The magazine caught Wendell Castle and ceramic artist Nancy Jurs living among their own work while much of it was still fresh from the studio.
‘Today, these works are usually seen in museums, but as furniture, they were made to be used,‘ Alison says. Her aim is to let visitors feel how the pieces functioned within the home.
Castle Home, circa 1970s | image courtesy Estate of Wendell Castle and Friedman Benda
the house becomes an archive
Across Friedman Benda‘s gallery space, enlarged photographs from the House Beautiful spread act like murals. Objects pictured in the designer‘s old rooms appear again in front of their own images, bringing the Scottsville interior into the present without turning it into a period reconstruction. The house occupied a former mill that Wendell Castle renovated, and its contents kept changing as work moved upstairs from the studio.
Alison has explained that pieces often entered the living space while waiting for a buyer, sometimes remaining with the family for years. Living with them gave her parents time to study what they had made and think through future work.
The house also recorded the creative world around Castle and Jurs. Their friends’ work entered through purchases and trades, including paintings by Michael Venezia and a ceramic fireplace by Roy Cartwright. Glenn Adamson’s catalogue essay also points to craft artists Tommy Simpson and Ann Sutton as part of the couple’s wider circle.
Alison remembers the atmosphere: ‘Our home became a total environment where furniture, ceramics, color and architecture blur together.‘ Castle appeared in both the wood and plastic sections of Objects: USA, the landmark 1969 Smithsonian exhibition that brought American studio craft to a much larger audience.
Wendell Castle: Living | image courtesy Friedman Benda and Wendell Castle Inc., photography by Izzy Leung
a career written into the grain
The installation also makes Castle’s technical evolution unusually easy to follow. His 1962 Chaise Rocker still lets the eye read oak members meeting through visible joinery, while another early chaise nearby carries the same sense of furniture assembled from distinct pieces.
In 1963, Castle began developing stack lamination, building timber into thick layered masses and carving them back into continuous forms. By Environment in 1972, stacked and laminated walnut had become architecture at the scale of furniture, with a bed and work surface absorbed into a broad horizontal wooden landscape. A lamp and drawers emerge from the same body.
Across the room, Opposites Attract (2017) turns that logic on its side. The massive floor lamp rises from diagonally oriented laminated wood, with a side table and drawer integrated into its body. The grain sweeps upward through the form, making the construction itself part of the visual movement.
Nearby, Arcadia (2010) turns a three-seat bench into one continuous carved body, its openings and raised ends giving the mahogany form an almost anatomical rhythm. Seen together, the works let the eye track decades of experimentation through the direction of the wood.
Wendell Castle: Living | image courtesy Friedman Benda and Wendell Castle Inc., photography by Izzy Leung
family furniture keeps its traces
Some of the most affecting objects are also among the smallest. Castle made a wooden high chair for Alison, carving her name across the back in broad graphic lettering. Elsewhere, a 1973 coat rack carries his own hat, still covered with wood shavings from his final time working in the studio. These details place biography directly onto the furniture. The high chair belongs to childhood; the hat still seems to belong to the workshop.
Nancy Jurs’ presence runs throughout the rooms with equal ease. Her ceramics sit on tables and shelves, echoing the vessels visible throughout the 1973 magazine spread, while friends’ artworks keep the installation open to a wider creative circle.
Jurs would later move further into sculptural ceramics, including her Wall Pouches of the 1980s, but here her vessels retain their place within the household. In the old photographs, Castle’s bright molded seating shares rugs and tabletops with handmade ceramics. Friedman Benda brings that visual density back into the room.
Wendell Castle: Living | image courtesy Friedman Benda and Wendell Castle Inc., photography by Izzy Leung
kermit on a masterpiece
The Kermit toy on Environment may be the detail that explains the whole exhibition best. The piece is huge and technically ambitious, yet here it becomes a bed again. Family videos flicker nearby. Alison’s curatorial premise comes through in these small collisions between canon and use, where a major work can hold a childhood toy and a gallery can briefly take on the looseness of a family room.
By the time Wendell Castle: Living reaches Castle’s later works, the exhibition has become both a chronology and a portrait of the world around the objects. You can follow changes in woodworking through the seams, then look up and find Jurs’ ceramics or a friend’s painting nearby. Before these works entered museum collections and design histories, people sat in them and slept beside them. At Friedman Benda, that earlier life comes back into view.
Wendell Castle: Living | image courtesy Friedman Benda and Wendell Castle Inc., photography by Izzy Leung
Wendell Castle: Living | image courtesy Friedman Benda and Wendell Castle Inc., photography by Izzy Leung
the first stop of our new travelling series brought together designers, architects, collaborators, and friends for a week of conversations and hands-on activities.

Sikh trucker stabbed in Wyoming, stirring fresh fears in US community

The stabbing of a truck driver at a remote Wyoming rest stop had US Sikhs on edge on Friday amid rising anti-immigrant vitriol against the community and its truck drivers in particular.
The Sikh victim was attacked from behind early Sunday while in a restroom at the Bitter Creek rest stop on Interstate 80 midway between Cheyenne and Salt Lake City, according to court documents. He suffered stabs to the neck and chest and over a dozen other cuts but survived.
While police say the motive is unknown, the attack came after deadly crashes involving Sikh truck drivers led to debate about commercial driver’s licensing requirements – sparking hatred towards Sikhs as a group, community leaders said.
Anti-Sikh sentiment has been especially severe on truck-driving forums, said one Sikh in the trucking industry, Harsimran Singh, CEO of Gillson Trucking in Stockton, California.

Senior US officials to 'Post': Trump-Netanyahu meeting not currently planned at UNGA
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-18
23:41:33 UTC
08:41:33 KST

A meeting between US President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is not currently on the agenda during Netanyahu's upcoming visit to the United States, a senior US official told The Jerusalem Post on Saturday, with the latest schedules placing the two leaders in New York at different times.
Netanyahu's presence in New York is expected to be "quite limited," the official said, noting that under the most recent schedule available to the administration, the prime minister is not due to arrive until after Trump has already left.
"The latest scheduling that I've seen, he will be here after the president leaves," the official said when asked directly whether Netanyahu was seeking a meeting with Trump.
A senior Israeli official told the Post that Netanyahu is expected to arrive in New York on the morning of his UN General Assembly address and depart for Israel immediately afterward.
At this stage, it appears Netanyahu will fly directly from Israel to New York rather than stop in Texas, and may not spend a night in the United States at all. However, the source stressed that the prime minister’s final itinerary has not yet been finalized.
Netanyahu's UN General Assembly address is expected later in the week, the US official added, while Trump is set to arrive in New York on Monday and depart Tuesday evening.
The US official declined to say whether Netanyahu or members of his team had formally requested a meeting, citing a policy against discussing requests submitted to the White House. In practical terms, however, the current schedule leaves no overlap between the two leaders' time in the city.
The UN's 81st General Debate runs September 22–28 at UN headquarters in New York.
Iran, Gaza at center of Trump's UN agenda
Even without a Netanyahu meeting, Israel and the Middle East are expected to feature prominently across Trump's UN visit.
US Ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz said Trump plans to stress in his General Assembly address that Iran must never obtain a nuclear weapon, while also highlighting what the administration views as progress under the president's 20-point Gaza peace plan.
Iran is also expected to loom large in Trump's multilateral meeting with leaders of the Gulf Cooperation Council. A senior US official said Tehran would be "a key topic of conversation and diplomacy" throughout the week.
The administration believes pressure on Iran continues to mount, the official said, arguing that Tehran's leverage over the Strait of Hormuz is diminishing as alternative infrastructure and bypass routes come online, compounded by US military and economic pressure. "In one way or another," the official said, Washington expects the Iranian regime to abandon its pursuit of a nuclear weapon.
Officials added that US sanctions against Chinese and Hong Kong entities accused of helping Iran generate revenue - including through oil-related activity - would continue.
Waltz also tied the UN gathering to Gaza, calling the annual session an unusually valuable diplomatic opportunity given the concentration of world leaders in one place.
Trump's publicly announced Tuesday schedule includes bilateral meetings with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, a sit-down with GCC leaders, and a reception for world leaders - but no meeting with Netanyahu. AP separately reported the planned meetings with Burnham, Takaichi and the Gulf leaders.
From New York to Xi Jinping meeting
Immediately after Trump's UN appearance, the diplomatic spotlight shifts to Washington, where the president is set to host Chinese President Xi Jinping for a three-day visit.
On Wednesday, Trump is scheduled to greet Xi and his wife at Joint Base Andrews. The following day, Trump and First Lady Melania Trump are expected to formally welcome the Chinese couple to the White House; after an arrival ceremony, the two leaders will review a military ceremony in the Rose Garden before holding bilateral talks. That evening, the president and first lady will host the Chinese delegation for a state dinner in the East Room.
On Friday, the two couples are expected to hold a private tea at the White House before visiting the National Archives to view founding US documents as the country marks its 250th anniversary.
The visit follows Trump's meeting with Xi in China in May; Trump had previously announced Xi's US visit for September 24.
Several of the most sensitive issues in US-China relations are expected to be on the table. A senior White House official confirmed that artificial intelligence and the current US-China trade truce will be discussed, alongside trade, AI, and rare-earth exports - all expected to feature prominently in preparatory talks between senior US and Chinese officials.
The administration also intends to press China over precursor chemicals used in fentanyl production, rare-earth supplies, and the terms under which Chinese investment can enter the United States. The White House made clear it does not intend to trade away US export controls in exchange for rare earths it believes Beijing has already committed to supply - though officials confirmed discussions have taken place over possible tariff reductions on a "narrow band" of non-sensitive, non-strategic goods.
Musk, Bezos, Altman, Cook in the same room
The state dinner's guest list is expected to draw nearly as much attention as the summit itself.
A senior White House official said expected attendees include Jeff Bezos, Elon Musk, Google CEO Sundar Pichai, Michael Dell, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser and Apple CEO Tim Cook, alongside senior administration officials. "It'll be a very popular and hot-ticketed event here in Washington, DC," the official said.
Several major tech executives are indeed expected to attend, while Reuters has reported that Xi may bring a substantial Chinese business delegation of his own.
Within the span of a few days, then, Trump will pivot from Iran, Gaza and the Gulf in the corridors of the United Nations to America's most consequential strategic rivalry - with China, trade, artificial intelligence and Iran all converging on the White House agenda.

Ukrzaliznytsia clarifies new operating rules based on air threat levels
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-18
23:40:00 UTC
08:40:00 KST

Ukrzaliznytsia clarifies new operating rules based on air threat levels
JSC Ukrzaliznytsia announced this via Telegram, Ukrinform reports.
Under the new rules, trains will continue to operate during a "yellow" threat level. Receiving and dispatching trains, as well as other operational processes – including passenger boarding and alighting at railway terminals, stations, and platforms – will be permitted.
Passengers may choose whether to remain at terminals and stations. They will be informed of the threat level and the location of the nearest shelters.
In the event of a "red" threat level, passenger boarding and alighting will be suspended. Passengers, railway staff, and other visitors will be moved to the nearest shelters.
However, the movement of trains already en route will not automatically stop. Decisions regarding each train will be made individually, taking into account the operational situation and air threat information provided by Ukrzaliznytsia’s monitoring teams. If airborne targets posing a threat to passengers or railway staff are detected, the teams will promptly notify railway personnel, after which measures will be taken – if necessary – to move people to shelters or other safe locations.
Ukrzaliznytsia will also disperse passenger flows and rolling stock to prevent overcrowding. If necessary, the operation of specific trains may be restricted or temporarily suspended.
Passengers at railway stations and stops will receive additional information via loudspeakers, information displays, and the Ukrzaliznytsia website and mobile app. Guidelines on what to do during various threat levels, as well as routes to the nearest shelters, will also be published.
Additionally, provisions have been made to supply staff working directly with trains with extra personal protective equipment, such as protective vests and helmets.

25% youths in 250 districts not in education or jobs: Survey
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-18
23:31:28 UTC
08:31:28 KST

The situation is of particular concern in northernIndia (Representative image)
NEW DELHI: In nearly 250 districts, more than 25% youth (15-29 age group) are neither engaged in any productive work, nor are they pursuing education or any sort of training for work, highlighting a gap in human capital utilisation.The situation is of particular concern in northern India, especially in states such as Bihar, UP, Haryana, Punjab and West Bengal, where nearly two-thirds of districts have around a quarter of the young population categorised as NEET (not in employment, education or training), showed the first-ever district-level periodic labour force survey (PLFS) for 2025, released by statistics ministry Friday.In Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Assam and Telangana in nearly half the districts, 25% young population is categorised as NEET (not in employment, education or training). A recent Niti Aayog report pegged the number of NEET youth in the country at nearly nine crore, with govt clarifying that these people cannot be crudely termed as unemployed.In around 25 districts, NEET is below 10%, including Kabirdham, Rajnandgaon and Uttar Baster Kanker in Chhattisgarh; Chamba in Himachal Pradesh; Ernakulam in Kerala; and Mandla in Madhya Pradesh. Nabarangpur in Odisha had the lowest NEET rate of 4.1%.
The ministry's report covered around 600 districts in major states and UTs. In some cases, it clubbed a few adjoining districts and treated them as a single unit.
Lowest unemployment rates across India
Generally, high unemployment rate among youth is attributed to their participation in education or their engagement with skilling or vocational programmes. NEET, however, represents those people who are not enrolled anywhere with any educational institution and have also withdrawn from the labour force altogether. This is either due to them attending to domestic unpaid duties, care work in the case of women or those who have stopped looking for work due to no suitable work being available, or in some cases, preparing for exams or having leisure. For young women, nearly three-fourth of total districts surveyed recorded a NEET rate of more than 25%, highlighting the burden of unpaid domestic chores and societal expectations.

Gemini hacked 3 companies in first known breakout by Google’s AI: Wall Street Journal
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-18
